name: Stealing Bundles
description: Stealing Bundles (also known as Stealing the Old Man's Bundle) is a simple fishing card game for two or more players, popular with children. It is similar to Casino but simplified. Players capture face-up cards from the table by matching their rank. Captured cards are stacked in a 'bundle'. The unique twist is that players can steal an opponent's entire bundle by matching the top card.

history.origins: A children's fishing game also known as Steal the Old Man's Bundle or Steal Pile. A very similar game is played in Argentina as Casita Robada and in Italy as Rubamazzo. It is classified as a fishing game and shares capture-by-rank and bundle-building with games like Casino but is simplified for young players.
timeline: 1900s: Common in game compendiums for children.
Present: Still played as a starter card game.
history.cultural: A 'gotcha' game where fortunes change instantly.

setup.players: 2, 3 or 4 players. First dealer is chosen by everyone drawing a card; highest card deals (tied players draw again).
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack; suits are ignored for matching (only rank matters).
setup.dealing: Dealer gives each player 5 cards; remaining cards are dealt face-up to the table. Play starts to the left of the dealer.

rules.objective: Have the most cards in your bundle when all cards have been played; the player with the largest bundle wins.
rules.gameplay: Each turn a player plays one card from hand. They may (1) capture one or more table cards that match its rank and add them to their bundle, (2) steal an opponent's entire bundle by playing a card that matches the top card of that bundle (the stolen bundle is added to their own), or (3) trail by placing the card face-up on the table if they cannot or choose not to capture. Play continues until all hands are empty. The player with the most cards in their bundle wins.
keyRules: Capture table cards by matching rank; captured cards go to your bundle.
Steal an opponent's bundle by playing a card that matches the top card of their bundle.
If you cannot or do not capture, trail your card face-up to the table.
Most cards in your bundle at game end wins.

strategy.basic: Always steal a bundle if possible. It swings the score massively. If you have two cards of the same rank, play one to capture/steal? No, usually you only play one. If you have a match for a table card and a match for a bundle, take the bundle.
strategy.intermediate: Baiting: If you have two 8s and there's an 8 on the table, you might wait to capture if you think someone else will capture it, letting you steal their bundle next turn? Risky.
strategy.advanced: Tracking: Remember what opponents captured. If they stole a bundle with a King on top, the King is now covered by your stealing card (e.g., a 5). The King is buried.
tips: The top card of your bundle is your shield.
